chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ayub ibn Nuh from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Isma'il al-Ju'fi from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

In the case of a husband and two parents, he said: 'For the husband is half, and for the mother is one-third, and what remains is for the father.' And in the case of a wife and two parents, he said: 'For the wife is one-quarter, and for the mother is one-third, and what remains is for the father.'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided between a spouse, mother, and father in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the specific distribution of the 'residuary' portion (al-Asabah) to the father when the mother receives her fixed one-third share, a ruling that distinguishes the father's role as the primary male heir in this configuration. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential understanding of how the Quranic shares for spouses and parents interact, particularly emphasizing the mother's consistent one-third share regardless of whether the deceased is male or female, while the father inherits the balance.
